_comment: Explanatory blocks rendered underneath the interop matrix by
generate_compact_report.py. Edit the wording here; no Python changes needed.
Each entry in "blocks" becomes one card, laid out in a two-column grid in
the order given. A block has a "title" plus any combination of:
body    Paragraph text. A string, or a list of strings joined with a
single space so long prose can be line-wrapped for editing.
This is the ONLY field inserted as raw HTML, so inline tags
such as <strong> and <em> work here. Keep it to inline
formatting; anything untrusted must not go in this file.
links   Buttons below the body. "label" and "href" are required;
"icon" optionally names a built-in glyph (see LINK_ICONS in
the script; "github" is the only one today). http, https and
legend  Status key rows. "outcome" names a pytest result (Passed,
Failed, Error, Skipped) and pulls in the exact same glyph the
matrix cells use, so the key cannot drift from the table.

blocks.title: About this report
body: These results were generated by Findy Wallet Tester,
an open-source automated interoperability test suite against
Pensiondemo issuers and verifiers.
You can find more about them from the following links.

legend.description: The full protocol flow completed successfully end-to-end.
The flow did not complete. The wallet or agent rejected the request, timed out, or returned an unexpected response.
The test runner hit an unexpected exception before the flow could be evaluated. The result is inconclusive.

blocks.title: Reading the matrix
body: Rows are agents (issuer or verifier services);
columns are wallet apps. A cell shows whether the
wallet successfully completed a testing flow with an agent.
The Issuance section covers credential offer and acceptance;
Verification covers presentation requests and responses.
A passing diagonal (same vendor on both sides) does not imply
cross-vendor compatibility, meaning each cell is independent.

blocks.title: Questions or issues?
body: Results reflect a single automated run and may not capture all
real-world scenarios. Passed results reflect fully working
compatibility within testing limitations but failures can stem from
configuration differences, transient network conditions, or test
environment limitations rather than fundamental incompatibility.
If a result looks incorrect or there are wallets or agents which
should be added to testing suite, please raise an issue in the
Findy Wallet Tester Github repository.
We welcome feedback and contributions to the project.
